digest.component_or_area: source code comment hygiene and CI validation
propositions: Source code comments contain rot-prone references (commit SHAs, run IDs, dated incident narratives) that become unresolvable due to Gerrit rebase-on-submit and CI retention policies; 8+ of 18 cited SHAs in the tree are already unresolvable.

A detector must identify rot-prone patterns (SHA-like hex ≥7 chars, run/job/thread IDs ≥8 digits, date+incident-verb blocks) and accept only if the block cites a ticket/epic/story/bug ID or uses the 'context: external' escape hatch.
All detector hits at HEAD must be remediated by either deleting rot-prone tokens, citing a ticket system ID, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log.

A CI guard (scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py) must block reintroduction of rot-prone refs; it must reject false-positive patterns like 'bug surfaced' (current-state explanation, not historical narrative) and file-path-derived word-triple aliases, while accepting sentence-final aliases and 4x4 hex-grouped ticket IDs.
The detector's unit test module must be excluded from tree scans and contain live rot-prone fixtures as red/gotcha cases; the remediated tree must scan clean with zero in-tree suppressions.
